blurb: A type was named with a `.` and a member it does not have. `T.name` refers to a variant of the sum type `T` or to a static method declared on it, and a misspelt variant has no such member. Some built-in types have a closed set: `HttpResult`, `ErrorStatus` and `RoundingMode` only their variants, `Float` only `parse`, `pi` and `e`, and `Decimal` only `parse` and `fromInt`. Check the spelling against the declaration, or declare the missing static method.
example:
type Colour =
    | Red
    | Green

Colour.Gren          // ✗ `Colour` has no variant `Gren`

Colour.Green         // ✓ the declared variant
